title: Grill round 2: New Task redesign, push-back
summary:
Round 1 settled 23 of 24 items, and I accepted every one as given. **Three answers need one more decision**, because two of them pull against each other or against the code:

1. In **surfaces** you picked both *RunPanel send box: shared-primitive changes only* **and** *RunPanel send box: full redesign too*. Those are exclusive, so I need to know what "full" covers.
2. **Sections with collapsible summaries** plus your **frequent fields** list. You change Project, Isolate, Pipeline, Harness, Model and Effort on most tasks, and those are almost all of Workspace and Agent. Collapsing those sections would hide what you use most.
3. **Mode** isn't in your frequent list, but it got a dedicated segmented control. Where does it live?
proven: Round-1 decisions recorded as given: one shared launch picker, every drift item carried everywhere (gate Run included), a Code|Plan segmented control plus variant, a searchable harness picker, a resizable panel (default 384 px), a two-column dialog, the subtle selected style, one custom picker family, all three bugs fixed (handles skipped by the warning), **Run task** everywhere, primitives added additively on this branch, the full acceptance bar, and all 8 confirm defaults.

questions.title: You chose both 'shared changes only' and 'full redesign' for the RunPanel send box. What should this change do to it?
questions.why: A full redesign adds a second large surface (the send dock and its toolbar) to the plan and to e2e.
questions.context:
Round 1 answer: `surfaces` = [..., `runpanel-shared-only`, `runpanel-full`].

The send box is `PromptComposer` with `label={null}`, `placement="above"` and flattened spacing. Its toolbar carries **Save for later**, **Commit & push**, **Resolve conflicts** and **Send**, plus the drag-and-drop ring and the read-only 'Viewing a background agent' bar. A full redesign would restyle that toolbar and its buttons to the new pattern (subtle states, h-9, one picker family, rem text, Cmd/Ctrl+Enter parity).

options.label: Full redesign in this change: the dock, its toolbar actions and the background-agent bar adopt the new pattern
options.consequence: Bigger plan. RunPanel e2e specs are touched, and the send-box screenshots become before/after.

options.label: Shared changes only (it inherits the tokens, label association and text sizes through PromptComposer); the layout is unchanged
Shared changes now; the full send-box redesign is a separate ticket I'm deferring
options.consequence: Recorded as owner-deferred, with you as the decider.

recommendation.reason: You ticked it, and you usually prefer the complete path. It makes the composer look the same wherever you type a prompt.

questions.title: Your frequent fields cover most of Workspace and Agent. What should collapse?
questions.why: This decides the panel's default state, and whether a frequently used control can end up hidden behind a click.
questions.context:
Round 1: `ia` = **sections-summary**. `frequent-fields` = Type, Title, Prompt, Files, **Project, Isolate, Pipeline, Harness, Model, Effort**.

Not frequent: Branch name, Extensions (MCP · Skills…), Agent profile, **Mode**, Speed / Max Mode.

options.label: Sections are always open, and the frequent fields are always visible. The rare fields in each section sit behind a small **More options** disclosure, remembered in localStorage. No whole-section collapse
options.preview:
TASK       Type · Title · Prompt · Files
WORKSPACE  Project · Isolate
           ▸ More options (Branch name)
AGENT      Pipeline · Harness · Model · Effort
           ▸ More options (Agent profile, Mode, Speed, Max Mode)
options.consequence: Nothing you use often is ever hidden. The panel is still shorter than today.

options.label: Workspace and Agent can collapse to a summary line, but they start **expanded** and only collapse when you choose to (remembered)
options.consequence: Closest to round 1. The default length is the same as today, minus the regrouping.

options.label: Both: each section can collapse to its summary line, and inside an open section the rare fields sit behind More options
options.consequence: The most flexible, with two disclosure levels to build and test.

recommendation.reason: It keeps your round-1 summary-line choice and makes sure the open state never puts a frequent field behind a click.

questions.title: Where does the Code | Plan control sit, given that Mode isn't in your frequent list?

options.label: Always visible in Agent, under Harness (one row); only the variant picker goes into More options
options.consequence: Plan stays one click away; the variant (Auto / Accept edits / Ask) is behind the disclosure.

options.label: The whole Mode control (segmented + variant) goes into More options
options.consequence: A shorter Agent section; switching to Plan takes 2 clicks.

recommendation.reason: The segmented control is what makes Plan one click. Hiding it would defeat the reason it was chosen.
